subject: geom_boxplot() and base boxplot() disagree substantially on this vector...

messages.author: d994cff5897faec8
messages.subject: geom_boxplot() and base boxplot() disagree substantially on this vector...
parts:
# Given
X <- c(74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74,
74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 45,
5, 1337, 74, 74, 74, 74, 751, 751, 767, 767, 767, 90, 767, 90,
90, 767, 751, 90, 90, 767, 751, 751, 767, 90, 767)

> boxplot.stats(X)$stats
[1] 5.0 74.0 74.0 420.5 767.0

# compare
x11()
boxplot(X)
x11()
qplot(1, X, geom='boxplot')

I can't figure out how to extract numbers from stat_boxplot, but the
boxplot produced is profoundly different from what I get from base
graphics, and inspecting the grob, the upper whisker is being drawn
_inside_ the box, which makes me think there's an out-and-out bug here
rather than a statistical disagreement.

zw

messages.subject: Re: geom_boxplot() and base boxplot() disagree substantially on this vector...
parts:
Yes, this is a known issue with stat_boxplot... actually, it's sort of two issues wrapped up together:
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/108

Changing it over is pretty simple for data where each case is on one row -- the fivenum() function will do the calculations. The problem is that with weighted data, it's not clear where exactly the hinges should go.

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: geom_boxplot() and base boxplot() disagree substantially on this vector...
parts:
Hi Zack -

There were two issues here. One was that the whisker is drawn inside the box. This sometimes happened when the hinges of the box were interpolated, but now it's fixed.

The other issue is that it stat_boxplot() calculates the hinge positions differently from boxplot(). stat_boxplot uses straight quantiles (25% and 75%), while boxplot does something a little more complicated and depends on the exact number of observations. If you want more info, see:
  ?boxplot.stats
and:
  https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/108#issuecomment-3215602

I haven't been able to find any information suggesting that the method used by boxplot is better in any way. If anyone out there knows of any such information, please feel free to share.

-Winston
